samples.question: This picture contains exactly one navy compass rose and exactly one crimson arrow, drawn far apart on a plain background. The rose is the navy figure made of four separate solid tips placed at right angles around a common centre: exactly one tip is a triangle and the other three tips are squares. The navy triangular tip marks NORTH; going clockwise around the rose from the triangular tip, the three square tips mark EAST, then SOUTH, then WEST. The crimson arrow points along its own length, towards its wide triangular head and away from its narrow flat tail. Grey marks are decoration and must be ignored. Screen-up is not necessarily north: the rose is the only thing that fixes the compass directions. Assign the arrow to whichever of the four rose directions is closest in angle to the arrow's pointing direction. Which compass direction is the crimson arrow pointing? Answer north, east, south or west.
